title: Sell Mineral Rights in Loma, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Loma, CO | Mesa County Piceance Flank
metaDescription: Own minerals near Loma, CO in the Grand Valley? We check Piceance Basin gas history and older Mesa County well records before quoting your interest.
heroLead: Loma sits at the western edge of the Grand Valley, close to the Utah line, where Piceance Basin gas potential runs into a mix of historic oil shale ground and quieter conventional wells.
intro: Loma is a small unincorporated Mesa County community northwest of Fruita, an area better known historically for its proximity to the Naval Oil Shale Reserve lands than for conventional drilling density. If your family homesteaded or ranched around Loma, the minerals you hold likely trace back to that agricultural history rather than to a modern lease deal.

sections.heading: Piceance flank, not core
paragraphs: The dense Piceance Basin gas development that built up Garfield County towns like Rifle and Parachute doesn't extend with the same intensity into this part of Mesa County. Loma-area minerals are more likely tied to scattered conventional wells or to remain undrilled altogether, and the local oil shale history nearby means some of the value story here is speculative rather than production-based.
We check COGCC records specific to your section to see whether any well has ever been permitted or produced on your acreage before we build a valuation.

sections.heading: What we need from you
paragraphs: Your deed or legal description, and any division order statements if you've received royalty income in the past. Mesa County's clerk and recorder's office in Grand Junction holds the filings we'd need to trace ownership history if records are incomplete.

faqs.question: Is there active gas drilling near Loma right now?
faqs.answer: Development here is lighter than the Piceance core in Garfield County. We check current COGCC activity for your specific section rather than assuming based on the broader basin.

faqs.question: What does it mean that this area has oil shale history?
faqs.answer: Decades of federal oil shale research and reserve designation shaped land use here, though it never became commercial production. It's a different resource story from natural gas but sometimes affects title and land-use records.

faqs.question: Will you buy an interest that's never produced?
faqs.answer: Yes, priced as undeveloped acreage rather than an income-producing interest. We'll be clear about that distinction before quoting.

faqs.question: Is Loma's proximity to Utah relevant to my mineral value?
faqs.answer: Not directly — the geology and any producing history tied to your specific section matter far more than the county line. We check COGCC records regardless of how close you sit to the state border.

faqs.question: How long does an evaluation for undeveloped ground take?
faqs.answer: Usually just a few days once we have your legal description, since there's no production history to reconcile against multiple wells.
